messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT PAGE — p99 tail latency spike on inference streaming endpoints (/v1/stream/generate). Alerting oncall @sam. Automatic severity: P2. Metrics: p99 latency -> ~7.2s (baseline ~600ms). Traffic: steady. Potential customer impact: streaming stalls/retries. Please ACK and triage.

sam: ACK. I'm on it. Can folks grab p95/p99 across regions and check streaming stalls vs complete timeouts? Also confirm whether it's auth/tokenstore, config fetch, or DB dependent.

elaine: looking now. Early signal: spike correlates with increased 5xxs and 429s from `auth-service` and elevated config fetch latencies. p95 ~900ms, p99 ~7s. Stack traces show waits in `config-client` RPCs.

alex: I see bursts of `featureflag-service` calls in front of runtime — feature flag client doing fanout on every stream start. We had a new rollout yesterday (ff:streaming-cache-v2) at 01:12 UTC across prod. Could be related.

maria: infra metrics show the configstore (Cassandra read pool) had thundering reads around 01:20 UTC with spikes in read latency to ~300ms per call (normally ~15ms). Replica sync lag also increased for two nodes. Could be compaction churn plus the ff rollout.

kevin: support reports ~15 customer sessions with interrupted streams and a couple of in-app retries. No full data loss, just token emission stalls.

sam: immediate mitigation options: 1) roll back ff rollout, 2) enable local sticky cache for feature flags (TTL bump), 3) route streaming requests to fallback model variant that bypasses config checks, 4) increase auth token cache TTL/size. Which is least risky and fastest?

alex: fastest low-risk is to bump local flag cache TTL on runtime (no restart) and enable local fallback for unknown flags. Rolling back rollout is next but may take time to propagate. We can also short-circuit config fetch calls in call path.

elaine: I can flip runtime flag that enables local TTL=300s for `streaming-cache-v2`. Patching now.

elaine: PATCH applied: `ff.client.cache_ttl=300` for runtime clusters in prod. Watching metrics.

ops-runner: deploy-bot: applied runtime config change to service/runtime-prod-*/env=prod (no restart). Rollout status: 100%.

alex: after TTL bump, auth 429s dropped ~40% in last 90s. p99 down from 7.2s -> ~2.1s but still elevated. Some streams still show intermittent stalls.

maria: DB compaction still causing some IO pressure. I'm spinning up an extra Cassandra read-only instance in the region to help absorb reads — will take ~4m to join.

sam: good. Also please add a temporary rate-limit bypass for internal controlplane calls from runtime -> configstore (allowlist) for 10m. We need to avoid cascading backoffs.

maria: added allowlist rule for runtime service identity, TTL 10m. Confirmed in firewall/rate-limiter.

kevin: notifying affected customer success leads: short blip for streaming tokens; recommending customer-facing note: minor token delays, retry-safe. ETA for full mitigation?

alex: once the extra read node is up and we keep the TTL bump, I expect p99 closer to ~800-1200ms. If not, next step is rollback of ff rollout.

incident-bot: NOTE: escalation threshold reached — handing off to eng-runtime for deeper investigation. Paging @alex and @elaine for post-incident analysis and timeline. Create postmortem if P2 persists beyond 2 hours.

elaine: confirmed extra node joined cluster. Read latency back to ~25ms for most calls. p99 at 860ms now. I'll keep monitoring for 15m.

sam: customer impact summary for handoff: - window: 01:18–01:32 UTC (spike) - sustained elevated p99 until 01:40 UTC mitigation in place - affected: streaming endpoint token emission stalled for ~1–3s additional latency for many sessions, ~15 reported sessions with visible stalls, no data corruption - severity: P2 (customer-facing but contained)

kevin: Support note drafted: "We've observed a transient increase in streaming token latency due to config service read pressure tied to a feature flag rollout; we've applied mitigations and are closely monitoring. No customer data was affected."

alex: next steps / action items:
- (A1) Root cause investigation: audit ff rollout client behavior + config fetch patterns (assigned: alex)
- (A2) Postmortem + timeline + preventive: add server-side backoff + local cache fallback for streaming client (assigned: elaine)
- (A3) Infra: review compaction schedules and autoscaling thresholds for configstore (assigned: maria)
- (A4) Support comms follow-up: proactive email to affected customers after postmortem (assigned: kevin)

elaine: quick check: I'll add a temporary guard in runtime to short-circuit synchronous config fetch on hot path and default to cached values if the call exceeds 150ms. Rolling a small patch now.

ops-runner: deploy-bot: runtime guard patch rolled to 20% canary -> 100% in 60s. No errors in canary.

alex: logs show the guard avoided ~120 blocking calls. p99 stabilized at ~650ms. Looks good. I'll start compiling detailed traces for the postmortem.

maria: infra note: compaction windows overlapped with snapshot backups. We'll reschedule heavy compaction and increase read pool size by 30% during peak to prevent recurrence.

sam: handing off oncall to alex for follow-up investigation and postmortem. I'll mark incident P2 resolved for active mitigation; keep monitoring and report if regression.

alex: ACK takeover. I'll open an incident tracking ticket and start the postmortem draft. Will include metrics, traces, rollout timeline, and action owners.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied. Current p99 ~620ms. Status: monitoring. Incident handoff complete (from @sam to @alex).
summary: p99 tail latency spike on streaming due to configstore read fanout from feature flag rollout; mitigations: TTL bump, allowlist, extra read node, runtime guard. Handed from oncall to eng-runtime. Postmortem and infra adjustments planned.
